title: Design System: Tideglass — moonlit sea glass

display.purpose: Titles, greetings, chapter numerals, drop caps and figures (opsz auto, SOFT 30–100, WONK accents).

prose.purpose: Default reader text; Fraunces, Geist and Atkinson Hyperlegible Next are reader options; user settings remain authoritative.

mono.purpose: Tabular figures, chapter positions and timings.

shadows.purpose: Pearl counterpart; inherited through CSS variables.

components.name: Primary button
components.description: The principal action: an accent gradient pill with a lit edge, a hover sheen and a press ripple.

narrative.overview: A reading room at the edge of a night ocean: living water behind the pages, frosted glass chrome, an expressive old-style serif for titles, and motion that rises, washes and reveals like a tide.
keyCharacteristics: Tide (dark) and Pearl (light) themes share one token vocabulary; the accent hue is a user setting.
A WebGL tide, the focused book's aura and grain form the background; the room takes the book's colours.
Floating glass island, novel capsule, phone dock and reader capsules; ordinary cards are translucent without blur.
Fraunces display, Geist interface, Literata reading type.
Springs, rising entrances, view transitions and a calm reading surface; full reduced-motion parity.
rules: Only floating elements use backdrop blur.
Status is never conveyed by colour alone.
dos: **Do** use tokens so theme, accent and book atmosphere flow everywhere.
**Do** let covers, titles and prose carry the identity; keep controls quiet.
**Do** keep focus visible, targets ≥ 40px, and keyboard, touch and reduced-motion parity.
**Do** show loading, empty and failed states distinctly, with a recovery action.
**Do** verify Tide and Pearl, desktop and 390px mobile after shared changes.
donts: **Don't** add backdrop blur to ordinary cards or long lists.
**Don't** nest interactive controls inside book links.
**Don't** hide essential cover actions from keyboard or touch users.
**Don't** invent statistics, stages or artwork claims for decoration.
**Don't** apply fixed light-theme colours to theme-aware or reader-tone surfaces.
